choices.text: Olefin metathesis used as an intramolecular process, finding increased use in complex organic synthesis
Olefin metathesis between two different molecules to build a polymer
choices.why: That is the intermolecular use of metathesis, for polymer synthesis. RCM is intramolecular.

choices.text: Ring-opening of a strained cycloalkene to make a polymer
choices.why: That is ROMP (Section 31.5). RCM closes a ring rather than opening one.

choices.text: Removal of ethylene from an open-chain diene to make a long polymer
choices.why: That is ADMET (Section 31.5), which is intermolecular.

explanation: Olefin metathesis has been used mainly as an intermolecular process for polymer synthesis, but it is also finding increased use in complex organic synthesis as an intramolecular process, called ring-closing metathesis (RCM).

prompt: What is the optimum catalyst for ring-closing metathesis?

choices.why: That makes a Ziegler–Natta catalyst for linear and stereoregular polymers (Section 31.2).

choices.text: BF3 with a small amount of water
choices.why: That is an acid catalyst for cationic polymerization (Section 31.1).
Butyllithium is an anionic polymerization initiator (Section 31.1).

explanation: The optimum catalyst for ring-closing metathesis is an Ru(II) complex, and cyclic alkenes with up to 30 atoms in ring size are easily produced.

prompt: Ring-closing metathesis easily produces cyclic alkenes up to what ring size, in atoms?
explanation: Using an Ru(II) complex as catalyst, ring-closing metathesis easily produces cyclic alkenes with up to 30 atoms in ring size.
